drugs.name: Tecovirimat
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits an orthopoxvirus envelope protein needed for the release of new virions from infected cells
drugs.use: FDA-approved for smallpox; used off-label for severe mpox alongside supportive care and pain control

drugs.name: Vancomycin
drugs.mechanism: Glycopeptide that binds the D-alanine-D-alanine end of peptidoglycan precursors, blocking cell wall polymer assembly after the alanine racemase step; resistance now seen in E. faecium and some S. aureus
drugs.use: IV for MRSA, including MRSA HAP/VAP; given orally, with fidaxomicin as the other first-line choice, for C. difficile colitis; with imipenem and an aminoglycoside for severe HAP

drugs.name: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX)
drugs.mechanism: Sequential folate blockade: the sulfonamide (a PABA analog) inhibits dihydropteroate synthase and its partner inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, so no tetrahydrofolate for DNA synthesis
drugs.use: 3 days for uncomplicated cystitis (10-14 if complicated); drug of choice for Pneumocystis pneumonia; sinusitis or epiglottitis in penicillin allergy or suspected S. aureus

drugs.name: Penicillin and aminopenicillins (amoxicillin, ampicillin)
drugs.mechanism: Beta-lactams that inhibit the transpeptidases (PBPs) cross-linking peptidoglycan; useless against wall-less Mycoplasma and against MRSA's mecA-encoded PBP2a; clavulanate added against beta-lactamase
drugs.use: Strep pharyngitis with 4 Centor points (no test needed); first-line bacterial sinusitis and healthy-outpatient CAP; 7 days for bacteriuria in pregnancy; E. faecalis; neonatal UTI with gentamicin

drugs.name: Third-generation cephalosporins (ceftriaxone, cefotaxime)
drugs.mechanism: Beta-lactam transpeptidase (PBP) inhibitors with broad gram-negative reach; resistance now spreading in E. coli, K. pneumoniae and gonococci; no activity against MRSA, and enterococci are resistant
drugs.use: Empiric bacterial meningitis; IM dose for gonorrhea; febrile infant UTI (IM or IV); epiglottitis; inpatient CAP with a macrolide; acute pyelonephritis

drugs.name: Carbapenems (imipenem, meropenem)
drugs.mechanism: Broadest beta-lactams (ring fused to a distinct bicyclic nucleus); Enterobacterales resist via efflux, lower outer-membrane permeability and, above all, KPC, NDM and VIM beta-lactamases that clavulanate barely blocks
drugs.use: Last-resort agents for resistant Klebsiella, E. coli and Pseudomonas; antipseudomonal choice for HAP/VAP; kept in combination regimens for resistant Enterobacterales when the MIC is 4 or less
